Kate —

Thanks, this is helpful. Quick reply and I'll attach a short checklist. High‑level assumptions we typically validate in MAPs (we'll tailor to your traffic profile):

- Baseline tokens/request: use median and p95 from your eval prompts (you gave median ~320).
- Tokens/session: avg prompts/session * tokens/request (you estimated ~960 tokens/session).
- Effective tokens/$ (hosted): depends on model variant; for example, Redwood-curated Llama-3-70B-quant gives ~0.0005 $/1k tokens (example; we'll run exact numbers).
- Caching assumption: prefix/KV cache hit rate scenarios (low: 15%, base: 45%, high: 70%) — critical for expected spend.
- Batching: batch sizes of 1/4/8 have throughput vs latency tradeoffs; typical production batch target for chat UI is 3–5 to keep median latencies <200ms.
- Prefetch/pipeline: when you can prefetch completions for predictable flows (e.g., next suggestion), cost can drop but increases engineering complexity.

I'll attach a one‑page checklist and simulated ranges. Can you share a small eval set (10–20 representative conversations) so we can run a token distribution sweep? If you prefer, upload to the Drive link in the MAP folder and we'll run the sim.

I'll also loop in Jordan and Ben for the quant/ops assumptions.

Thanks — Naomi

Naomi Feldman

Looping in with a quick ops note and the numbers I'll use for the sim:

- Input token distribution: median 320, mean 410, p95 1200 (based on similar health workflows).
- Reply tokens: mean 180, p95 520.
- Requests/day: 12k sessions * 3 prompts = 36k requests/day => ~14.0M tokens/day baseline (mean).
- Cost baseline: using our verified Llama-3-70B-quant profile -> $0.005 per 1k tokens (hosted; example). That implies ~$70/day baseline.
- Cache scenarios reduce token volume at request level. e.g., 45% cache hit -> effective token volume ~7.7M/day -> ~$38/day.
- Batching: if we can batch at 4 requests average for reranking/async, kernel throughput improves 2–2.5x on dedicated; that reduces committed GPU cost but has latency implications for interactive UI.

Action: Ben and I will run the token-sweep sim on the sample eval set and attach prefetched sim output (prefetch_sim_results.csv). Naomi — if MedLytics can share 20 conversations by EOD tomorrow we can include the p99 and cost-bands in the MAP doc.

-Jordan

From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Quick technical clarifications for the MAP checklist and the pilot gating criteria:

1) Metric instrumentation: we need per-route token counters (input, output) + cache hit/miss tags. Can MedLytics expose a test route or share logs for a week? If not, we can instrument in the sandbox.

2) Caching model: prefix caching works well for templated flows; for open text we expect lower hit rates. We'll include both prefix and KV cache scenarios in the MAP.

3) Batching policy: propose a canary that runs async batch size=4 for non-critical suggestions, and sync batch size=1 for primary query. That preserves UX while giving ops savings.

4) Failure modes: include a fallback plan in MAP -> degrade to smaller model or apply stricter caching policy if spend exceeds upper bound.

I'll attach a short appendix with the sim parameters and a CSV of per-token cost bands.

-Ben
